open_points.subject: R0-54 import sources vs one-time closure
open_points.text: The sources are the instances on the VPS and on the test rig; the owner picks one for each import. ... The first successful import into production closes the operation for good.
open_points.question: If the first successful import closes the operation, how can data from both the VPS and the test rig reach production, and is that intended?
options: one import may name several sources at once
the operation closes only after each source has been imported once
only one source is ever imported; the other is abandoned
open_points.default_guess: One import takes the sources the owner selects, and the operation closes after that import.

open_points.subject: create a project / correct a project failures
open_points.text: a customer reference that is unknown or erased refused (R0-16)
open_points.question: Must naming a restricted customer (R0-51) or a customer whose relationship has ended (R0-57) be refused on create and on correct, as the decisions say, even though the table lists only unknown or erased?
options: refuse restricted and ended customers on create and on correct
refuse them on create only and allow keeping them on correct
open_points.default_guess: Refuse restricted and ended customers whenever a project newly names them, on both create and correct.

open_points.subject: R0-55 restriction scope
open_points.text: A restriction stops every operation that uses the restricted customer's personal data
open_points.question: Does the customer's personal data include the address and characteristics of the objects of its projects? That decides whether context, read project and list projects keep returning the address for a restricted customer's projects.
options: only the Customer record's contact data
the contact data plus the addresses and characteristics of its projects' objects
open_points.default_guess: Contact data only; object addresses keep flowing to services cleared for personal_data.

open_points.subject: restrict or lift a restriction
open_points.text: or no longer restricted where a lawful ground allows it
open_points.question: Does lifting a restriction require the owner to record the lawful ground? Is lifting without one refused, and is the ground audited?
options: a ground is required and stored
the owner's own judgement is enough and nothing is recorded
open_points.default_guess: Require a free-text ground, store it and audit it; refuse a lift without one.

open_points.subject: erase a customer's contact data vs retention holdback
open_points.text: until that date the data is not erased
open_points.question: Does an active holdback block the owner's explicit erase action, or only the automatic retention erasure?
options: block both
block only automatic erasure; explicit erase overrides
refuse an explicit erase until the holdback is removed
open_points.default_guess: A holdback blocks automatic erasure only; an explicit erase is refused while it is active, and the refusal names the holdback.

open_points.subject: automatic retention erasure
open_points.text: When the applicable period ends, Registry itself erases or anonymises the data
open_points.question: Where is the action of Registry erasing or anonymising data at the end of a period, with its trigger, output (audit entry) and failure? No row of the action table carries it.
options: add a system-actor row
model it as a row of the owner's reviewed actions
open_points.default_guess: Add a row with Registry as actor, triggered when a period or holdback expires, writing an audit entry for each erasure.

open_points.subject: R0-56 holdback expiry
open_points.text: When that date comes, the need to keep the data is assessed again: the owner records a new ground and date, or the data is erased.
open_points.question: If the owner does nothing when the holdback date passes, is the data erased automatically, or does it wait for the owner?
options: erased automatically
held until the owner decides, and flagged in the owner interface
open_points.default_guess: Flag the data to the owner and erase it automatically after a grace period, the period to be set in State 2.

open_points.subject: Network surface: owner interface vs VM Agent
open_points.text: the owner interface, reachable from outside only through the owner's VPN
open_points.question: Can VM Agent reach the owner interface over the network, for example its sign-in page? The service API is stated as never reachable from VM Agent, but the owner interface is not.
options: the owner interface is unreachable from VM Agent
it is reachable and protected by the owner credential only
open_points.default_guess: The owner interface is unreachable from VM Agent.

open_points.subject: onboard_object replacement
open_points.text: its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows
open_points.question: How can Kernel flows take over the role of onboard_object (creating projects and customers) when R0-41 says Kernel no longer creates projects and the agent never sees customers?
options: only the owner interface takes the role
Kernel flows take only the room and artifact parts
open_points.default_guess: The owner interface takes creation; Kernel flows take only rooms and pointers on granted projects.

open_points.subject: stored facts list
open_points.text: Registry stores only identity — projects, their objects and rooms, customers with their contact data — the project access of each agent session and its pending request, artifact pointers, and its own audit log.
open_points.question: Are registered sessions, retention holdbacks with their lawful grounds, relationship end dates, restriction marks, recorded purposes of kept identities (R0-52) and the import-closed flag covered by this "only" list, or are they missing from it?
options: extend the list
treat them as attributes of the listed records
open_points.default_guess: Extend the list explicitly with retention and restriction records and session registrations.

open_points.subject: request access / read session access for an unregistered session
open_points.text: request access to a project | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session | ... | —
open_points.question: What happens when Kernel requests access for a session that is not registered (R0-53 requires a registered session)?
options: refused as an unknown session
the session is registered implicitly

open_points.subject: Kernel acting outside a session
open_points.text: producer service; Cabinet Kernel only for the agent, on a project its session is granted
open_points.question: Does Kernel ever call Registry as a plain trusted service without naming a session, for example validate or list artifacts? Or does every Kernel call carry agent authority and a session?
options: every Kernel call names a session
Kernel also has a sessionless trusted-service scope
open_points.default_guess: Every Kernel call names a registered session; there is no sessionless Kernel scope.

open_points.subject: change the active project
open_points.text: the session's active project changes, which revokes nothing
open_points.question: Can the owner clear the active project, leaving none? And what happens to the active project when it is revoked?
options: revoking the active project clears it
revoking the active project is refused until another is made active
open_points.default_guess: The owner may clear it; revoking the active project clears it.
